title: How roller coasters work
examples: How does the coaster get so fast at the bottom?
What makes the coaster go up the first hill?
Are the loops dangerous for people?

explain.say: Today we learn how roller coasters move so fast. We will look at energy and forces.
Potential energy is stored energy due to height. The higher up you go, the more potential energy you have.
Kinetic energy is the energy of motion. When the coaster moves fast, it has lots of kinetic energy.
When the coaster drops, potential energy changes to kinetic energy. This conversion makes it speed up quickly.
Loops use momentum to keep the coaster going. The speed at the bottom helps it complete the circle shape.
G-force is the feeling of weight pushing you in a seat. It changes when you go up or down fast.

faq.q: Does the coaster use an engine to go up the first hill?
faq.a: No, the coaster uses a chain lift system to pull the cars up. This stores the initial potential energy.
asks: Is there a motor at the start?

faq.q: Why does the coaster slow down at the end?
faq.a: The brakes are used to safely slow the coaster down for the next ride. This removes the kinetic energy.
asks: What is the purpose of the brakes?
Do the brakes stop it completely?

faq.q: Is the speed at the bottom always the fastest part?
faq.a: Yes, because the height is converted into speed at the lowest point. This is where most of the kinetic energy is.
asks: Is the bottom the fastest spot?

faq.q: What is the difference between potential and kinetic energy?
faq.a: Potential energy is stored energy based on position, while kinetic energy is the energy of movement. They change into each other.

faq.q: Do you need to be at a certain height to ride?
faq.a: Yes, most coasters require you to reach a certain height to ensure enough potential energy for the ride. Safety is very important.
asks: How high do I need to be?

facts: Potential energy depends on the height of the roller coaster.
Kinetic energy depends on how fast the roller coaster is moving.
The conversion from potential to kinetic energy happens during the drop.
Brakes are essential safety components that remove excess energy.

quiz.say: If a coaster is at its highest point, what type of energy does it have the most of?
quiz.why: At the highest point, the coaster has maximum height, meaning maximum stored potential energy.

wrong.0: Work energy is done by a force over distance, not the primary energy type stored at height.
wrong.2: Kinetic energy is about motion; at the top, the coaster is momentarily still.
wrong.3: Gravitational force is always pulling, but it is not the type of energy stored.

quiz.say: When a coaster moves from a high point to a low point, what happens to its energy?

options.show: Potential energy converts to kinetic energy
options.say: Potential energy converts to kinetic energy

quiz.why: The stored energy from height changes into the energy of movement as it drops.

wrong.1: Some energy is lost to friction, but the main conversion is PE to KE.
wrong.2: The height is changing, so the stored potential energy must change too.
wrong.3: You must start with potential energy from the lift hill to begin the motion.

quiz.say: If the brakes are working correctly, what do they remove from the coaster?
quiz.why: The brakes slow the coaster down by removing its energy of motion.

wrong.1: Brakes slow it down horizontally, not by changing its height.
wrong.2: Stored energy is related to height, which the brakes do not affect.
wrong.3: Gravity is always pulling; the brakes remove the energy of motion, not the force of gravity.
